recipes.name: Grilled Greek Yogurt Marinated Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 (5 pound) whole chicken, cut into 8 pieces

steps.text: Whisk together yogurt, garlic, lemon juice and zest, olive oil, paprika, herbes de Provence, salt, and black pepper in a medium bowl.
Pour into a large resealable plastic bag. Add chicken; stir to coat. Squeeze out excess air and seal the bag. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 3 hours.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate. Make sauce: Stir together yogurt, lemon juice, and harissa in a small bowl until combined. Set aside.
Remove chicken to a plate or baking sheet lined with paper towels; discard marinade. Pat chicken dry with more paper towels. Season with a pinch of salt.
Grill chicken, skin-side down, on the preheated grill for 2 minutes. Turn over each piece and move to indirect heat.

Continue grilling, turning often, with the lid down until well browned and meat is no longer pink in the center, 30 to 35 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the thigh, near the bone, should read 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).
Serve chicken with sauce on the side.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Greek Yogurt Marinated Chicken
raw_recipe.description: This Greek yogurt marinade with lemon, garlic, and herbs is from Chef John. It makes the most amazing grilled chicken you'll want to make all summer long!

review.reviewBody:
Wallaceclan - harissa is a North African chili paste. If you don't have it, you could make a paste with 1 t. sriracha or chili garlic sauce, 1 clove of crushed garlic, 1/2 t ground cumin , 1/2 t. ground coriander and 1/2 t. salt. 
This makes a very moist and flavorful chicken. I marinated for about 6 hours and it was perfect.

we thought this was very moist and flavorful.. i did deviate from the recipe a bit as i started marinating this in the morning for dinner then changed my mind a couple of nights in a row.. so this basically sat in the marinade for 48+ hours.. i used Herbs de Provence from this site for the seasoning (minus the lavender in it) and upped it to 1.5 tsp.. i only had boneless skinless thighs (1.5 lbs).. we cooked this on a conventional george foreman.. but it required a lot of attention to not burn it.. regular grilling would be the way to go.. lastly, we didn't bother with the yogurt/harissa sauce.. it was delicious as is.. ty for the recipe

Chef John is the best! Love his recipes and videos. 
I marinated boneless chicken pieces till the next evening. Dinner plans changed. It is April 6, but winter has made a comeback in Rhode Island. So I used the oven. 375' degrees, about 20 minutes. I used a rack on foil lined baking sheet. Flipped pieces once. Perfect. Marinade made them very moist and full of flavor, absolutely delicious. Mixed yogurt, mayonnaise and hot sauce for dipping. Not too bad! I will definitely make this again and again.

I made this pretty much "as written" - which I never do. My tweaks were: A 7 oz. container of lower fat Greek Yogurt - 3 lbs. of boneless, skinless chicken thighs and I added a Tablespoon of Granulated Onion. I marinated it all day in a giant Tupperware that I would flip every other hour. I did not remove the marinade at grill time and just sprayed our BBQ with some Pam for Grilling. DELISH! I did not make the dipping sauce - didn't need it. Served this with a cucumber and heirloom tomato salad and green beans. Healthy and delicious. There is a reason I follow Chef John on AR. Will definitely make this again! Something different to do with chicken! Yea!

I substituted preserved lemon for the lemon zest and used chicken thighs (don't really care for white meat). I grilled it indoors on a Cuisinart Griddler because it was raining. I cooked it to almost 160 degrees on the griddler and then put it under the broiler for 3 minutes to finish. I did not pat it dry so no need for a dipping sauce. It was delicious. It will be even better on the grill next time I'm sure. Although I routinely cook things with complex layers of flavor like a Louisiana court bouillon or gumbo, I seem to have difficulty turning out a decent grilled chicken dish. But this worked beautifully for me.

I have eaten A LOT of grilled chicken, and this was among the best. Served at a dinner party and everyone raved. I used boneless, skinless breasts instead of a whole chicken. And, I didn't pat dry the marinade, but just placed on the grill fully covered in the marinade. Also, the marinade itself tastes great, so before I coated the chicken, I set aside and chilled some of the marinade and used it as a sauce/condiment. Placed a dollop on the plate for dipping.

I enjoyed this recipe. I made it as directed with the exception of the herbes de provence, since I didn't have any. Instead, I added a little rosemary, oregano, and basil, which was all I had that seems to be ingredients in the herbes de provence. I also used a cast iron grill pan on the stove since I don't have an outdoor grill. As some others have said they left the marinade on the chicken and it turned out well, I decided to try it. The chicken browned up nicely and had great grill marks. Some have remarked that the chicken was bland, but I found it incredibly flavorful, probably because of the marinate being left on. It wasn't dripping with the marinade, but there was a good coating left on the chicken. It was so tender, I didn't need a knife. I used chicken tenderloins. I didn't make the dipping sauce because I didn't have enough yogurt and I didn't think it would need it with the marinade left on the chicken. But, I can say I've had a similar sauce in another dish (Moroccan Chicken) and it was very tasty. I'm sure it would have been tasty here too. I served the chicken with a side of couscous seasoned with a little lemon zest, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. The leftover zest I had and juice of the other half of the lemon I had not used in the marinade were enough.***To those unfamiliar with Harissa, you can buy it at any store. It's made from different peppers. My Meijer carries it in a powder form with all of the other spices and in a jar as a sauce

First, the yogurt grilled chicken could stand alone, but if you didn't like the harissa sauce you didn't add enough. My brother-in-law from Tunisia introduced us to harissa and this lemon yogurt dip was fabulous. I added garlic and triple the harissa. The entire family devoured it and demanded I make more to smear our bread in. Don't shortcut the marinating...I slathered each piece of chicken and set them in a pie plate for a few hours. This one is a must make again!

It was good. The sauce was good too. Didn't have harissa so used another's suggestion and mixed 1/2 tsp sriracha, 1 clove of minced garlic, 1/4 tsp ground cumin, 1/2 tsp ground coriander, and 1/4 tsp salt as the harissa to add with the yogurt and lemon juice; I didn't add more salt. It wasn't something I'm dying to make again. I did bake it at 350 degrees for about 35 minutes, so may be better on the grill.
I made it for hubby and I, only did two bone in breasts, so I kept about three tablespoons of sauce to the side, added a little honey, sriracha and a little cumin. Delicious sauce for dipping.
Made it a couple of times already, love it. I use skinless chicken breast that I flattened with a mallet, this way it cooks evenly. This is a really good recipe!!!!
Very good
Didn't make the harissa sauce and baked in the oven.

I had to improvise for the dipping sauce since I had no harrisa, so I used sriracha, garlic, salt and honey. OMG, this sauce could be used on absolutely anything and it was at our dinner. We put it on the veggies, mashed potatoes and pierogis. I also used a touch of pecan while grilling and the chicken was magnificent!

Fantastic, easy, flavorful marinade. I bet it is even better on salmon. I let the chicken marinate for about 90 minutes before cooking. I did not make the accompanying sauce. I made this as part of a quick, healthy weeknight meal. Just chicken and a green veggie salad. I ate the leftovers for lunch the next day and felt great. Would definitely make again. Modifications: Used zero fat Greek yogurt (just happened to be what was available at the store that afternoon). I was a little short on the 6 tbsp of lemon juice due to having small lemons.

Very good. I did it with chicken breast that I pounded out to make thinner. Cooked it indoor on the grill side of the Viking Range Portable Griddle/Grill. Was only able to let marinate about 30 minutes and it was still moist with good flavor. Can only imagine it would’ve been better with the minimum 3 hour marinade. Served it with quartered mini golden potatoes herbed and baked with olive oil; along with okra patties sautéed in iron skillet. Also made the sauce. While I would make the sauce again, the chicken had good flavor and moisture without it.
Family favorite

I made this Monday with chicken thighs, Greek seasoned potatoes, Brussels Sprouts. So good I am making again today with rest of Chicken thighs, rice and seasoned green beans. Thank you for your recipe. Note: I did not have harissa sauce nor did I make homemade harissa sauce. I did do yogurt with lemon juice, and I liked it
Excellent recipe!!! :)

Terrific! I made as written and the marinade produced such a deliciously moist chicken that had a great depth of flavor. The yogurt sauce on the side was an excellent addition. The husband did an excellent job grilling and was excited for the leftovers repurposed into chicken salad for lunch. Definitely a go-to recipe for grilled chicken. Thanks, Chef John!
